name: REBELLO, Leon

headline.note: First-person and professional sources establish early Department of Parliamentary Services attendant work, excluded ministerial staffing for Julie Bishop, and about six years of private foreign-investment legal practice at King & Wood Mallesons before the 2025 election. Published sources do not give exact appointment/cessation, hours, leave, admission timing or transitions, and the official biography reduces the history to 'Solicitor'. Governance and elected office are excluded, so no public/private full-time total is calculated.

career_spells.employer: Australian and overseas universities not fully identified
career_spells.evidence_note: Party biography identifies law and international-relations degrees and study in Australia, France and the Netherlands, but does not name every institution or provide dates.

Rebello's member biography and first speech describe work as a parliamentary attendant sorting mail and supporting the House chamber. In a 2026 interview he said he was about 19, and a later post described the work as roughly ten years before 2025. Exact dates, hours, employment basis and leave are unpublished.
career_spells.counting_note: Public employment is supported, but no countable full-time interval is established.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Minister for Foreign Affairs, the Hon. Julie Bishop MP
career_spells.evidence_note: Party, member, professional and first-person sources identify work on Julie Bishop's ministerial staff; Rebello recalled taking the role at about age 21. Exact title, appointment/cessation, hours and leave are not published.
career_spells.counting_note: Political staff employment is excluded irrespective of public funding.

career_spells.role: Solicitor, specialising in foreign investment law
career_spells.evidence_note: The official biography says only 'Solicitor'. Rebello and party profiles identify King & Wood Mallesons and foreign-investment specialization; a March 2025 Lawyers Weekly profile says he had worked there for the past six years and remained a solicitor while campaigning. Exact start, admission, hours, leave, secondments and cessation are unpublished.
career_spells.counting_note: Substantive private legal work is clear, but an approximate aggregate duration does not establish a precise continuous full-time interval.

career_spells.employer: Multicultural Communities Council Gold Coast / Cura Aged Care
career_spells.evidence_note: The organisation's 2023–24 and 2024–25 annual reports list Rebello as a director and describe his legal and ministerial-staff background. Appointment/cessation, remuneration and time commitment are not provided.
Official records show election to the House of Representatives for McPherson on 3 May 2025.
